actions.description: The declared re-enable after a safety reset: publish a zero Twist on /cmd_vel, then unpause the Gazebo world with /gazebo/unpause_physics. WPRPlugin keeps the last cmd_vel it stored and applies it as soon as the world runs; the zero replaces it, but it is an unacknowledged publication, so a stored command can still act for a few world steps.
actions.name: resume_simulation

outputs.description: True when the zero Twist was handed to rosbridge before the unpause; a transmission, not a confirmation
outputs.name: zero_command_published

facts.text: WPRPlugin::Load assigns the default command topic literal "cmd_vel" to command_topic_.
WPRPlugin::Load assigns the default odometry topic literal "odom" to odometry_topic_.
The plugin header includes the generated geometry_msgs/Twist and nav_msgs/Odometry headers.
The plugin creates a geometry_msgs::Twist subscriber on command_topic_ and advertises a nav_msgs::Odometry publisher on odometry_topic_.
WPRPlugin::cmdVelCallback stores linear.x, linear.y and angular.z in x_, y_ and rot_ under the plugin lock and sends no acknowledgement.

On every world update WPRPlugin::UpdateChild adds a yaw torque from the difference between the world yaw rate and rot_ and relative forces from x_ and y_ minus the relative linear velocity, each times its p gain, and publishes odometry when more than 1/odometry_rate_ of simulated time has passed.
The shipped wpb_home.model configures the WPR plugin with commandTopic cmd_vel and odometryTopic odom and no robotNamespace override.
wpb_home_sim advertises the absolute /wpb_home/pose_diff topic with the geometry_msgs::Pose2D type.

In a 20 Hz loop, when the /pose_reset to /base_footprint transform is available within 1 s, wpb_home_sim publishes pose_diff with x and y set to 0.9 times that transform's translation and theta set to its yaw minus pose_reset.theta.
wpb_home_sim subscribes to /wpb_home/mani_ctrl, /wpb_home/ctrl and /odom.
A /wpb_home/ctrl message containing 'pose_diff reset' sets pose_reset to the current odometry pose, and every /odom message re-broadcasts the /odom to /pose_reset transform.
wpb_home_controllers.launch starts the wpb_home_sim node.
The shipped wpb_simple.launch starts the Gazebo empty_world include with paused=false and use_sim_time=true.
WPRPlugin connects UpdateChild to the world-update begin event.
WPRPlugin::QueueThread serves the plugin's callback queue with a 0.01 s wall-clock wait while the plugin is alive and its node handle is ok.
wpb_simple.launch includes gazebo_ros's empty_world.launch.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service unpause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses with no physics step, pacing or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /cmd_vel, /odom and /wpb_home/pose_diff endpoints and the three companion Gazebo services and runs no Gazebo physics, WPRPlugin controller, wpb_home_sim node or wall-clock loop
odometry and pose-difference samples are placeholders and do not establish a trajectory, sensor frame, collision state or timing

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets, /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports and /gazebo/unpause_physics clears; it runs no Gazebo World::Step, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders

while paused, a live Gazebo runs no world update, so /odom (published from UpdateChild) and /clock are silent and an odometry read fails NOT_READY after its 2 s timeout; the fake silences /odom while its flag is set, the same way

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS client; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held; a graph without gazebo_ros has neither service
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.9.3 (Noetic) and 11 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions

the resume publishes a zero Twist before the unpause; it is unacknowledged and the plugin handles it on its own queue thread, so the stored command may act for a few world steps before it is replaced, and any other publisher of /cmd_vel (a teleop or navigation node) can store a new command at any time
the shipped Gazebo world and robot model are deployment choices; the declaration assumes the root namespace used by the shipped wpb_simple/wpb_home_mani launch files

WPRPlugin has no command timeout: it applies the last stored x_, y_ and rot_ at every world update (wpr_plugin.cpp:186-207, 237-243), so one MHS publication keeps the simulated base moving until another command arrives

/wpb_home/pose_diff is published only by wpb_home_sim, which only wpb_home_controllers.launch starts (included by wpb_home_mani, wpb_scene_1 and wpb_table, not by wpb_simple.launch); a reviewer probe with that topic silent showed mhs.resource.read failing NOT_READY after 2 s and each command waiting 2 s, so the reviewer removed pose_diff from the resource and kept it only as the explicit read capability; /odom left the resource for the same reason once the e-stop became the world pause (the device resource reads no topic, and the cmd_vel receipt reports the values it sent)

pose_diff passes an upstream convention through unchanged: x and y are 0.9 times the /pose_reset to /base_footprint translation (wpb_home_sim.cpp:181-182), measured from the frame of the last 'pose_diff reset' message; before the first reset that frame comes from a default-constructed static tf::Transform (wpb_home_sim.cpp:57)

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back: no world update runs, so WPRPlugin applies no force and /odom is silent; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill, and it holds until the resume command, the Gazebo GUI or another client unpauses the world (a GUI step advances it), and the plugin keeps its stored cmd_vel, which the resume zeroes first without an acknowledgement.
